inputIntegrity: Movement and interaction use Chromium Input.dispatchTouchEvent and native touchscreen taps; no keyboard movement or synthetic PointerEvents.
Read-only capture checks isTrusted=true and pointerType=touch for every observed pointer event; each selective lift verifies the corresponding native pointer ID.
The simulator winning receipt contains 38 trusted touch events and 19 pointerdowns. Its report records all objectives completed, 16 admitted simulated samples and a 15.55-second active win.

Controlled BLE uses only the existing injected navigator.bluetooth boundary with real EventTarget/DataView notifications. Five 70 BPM calibration packets span 4 seconds; no calibration value is replayed, one new gameplay packet is recorded, and device identity getters remain unread.
Actual JSON downloads and native localStorage verify source-labelled wins, simulator preferences/best persistence, and unchanged simulator preferences for the BLE win.
limitations: Native hidden-document transitions could not be exercised by tab activation/window minimization in this headless fixture. The six new cases cover native touch Pause/Resume and touchCancel; existing separately controlled lifecycle tests are not relabelled native-hidden evidence.
Physical smartwatch compatibility and measurement accuracy remain unverified in https://github.com/twangyal/projects-monorepo/issues/62.
Touchscreen and Bluetooth provider emulation establish browser software behavior, not physical Android/iOS touch behavior, watch compatibility, physiology or emotion inference.
No CI result is included. Temporary log paths identify original observations but are not durable links; only the selected byte-exact artifacts below are archived.
